ac:rich-text-body.p: Scope: the AS-IS manuscript flow from upload in ACS Publishing Center to handoff to DOTS, as it bears on Triage and Routing. Source: Manuscript_Flow_Publishing_TO_BE v1.1 (AS-IS slides: End to End, Who Does What, Sequence of Activities; Gaps; Proposed TO-BE), which reads the GEO workflow board in Miro (main flow). Updated 25 Nov 2026.

p: Six stages across four systems take a manuscript from upload to operations. Two compliance gates run before peer review, and a manuscript can leave the flow or loop back at four points.

p.em: Figure AS-1: AS-IS functional flow, upload to operations (schematic)

li.p: Systems: ACS Publishing Center (upload), ACS Paragon Plus (compliance checks, peer review), ServiceNow (ticket validation, admin check) and DOTS (operations). Each holds part of the manuscript status.

Compliance gate (G1): Paragon Plus checks OFAC lists (SDN, inclusion, exclusion) and rights retention / AAM language and top federal funders. A hit raises a ServiceNow ticket; no hit goes straight to the admin check.
Admin gate (G2): the first ServiceNow task is Admin Check or Assign EE. Missing items put the manuscript on hold while the author is contacted; if they are not corrected, it is unsubmitted.
Editor decision (G3): after peer review the editor accepts, asks for revision, rejects or transfers. Accepted manuscripts go to DOTS.

Exits and loops: rejected by Legal (confirmed OFAC match), unsubmitted (missing items), rejected or transferred (editor decision), and revision or reject-and-resubmit, which takes a Full Check and re-enters the flow.

p: The table follows the main path step by step, with the decision points and exits from the AS-IS sequence of activities.

td.p: Metadata extracted; record opened in Paragon Plus

No hit: go to step 8. Hit: go to step 5 or 6

Cleared or false positive: step 8. Not cleared: step 7
RRS / funder hit: ServiceNow ticket; vendor validates and contacts the author; adds an R flag or note for the EO
Flag or note on the manuscript; step 8
First task in ServiceNow: Admin Check or Assign EE
Manuscript admin checks: completeness of the submission
On hold: outreach to the author; corrected items return to Admin Check. Not corrected: unsubmitted
Profile validation: author lists, ORCID, emails, reviewer badges
iThenticate, Fundref and data checks (vendor re-runs iThenticate and funding data on revisions)
Editor decision: accept, revise, reject or transfer
Accept: step 14. Revise or reject-and-resubmit: step 15. Reject: end. Transfer: another journal
Accepted manuscript handed to DOTS; Operations takes over
Full Check on the revised manuscript, then it re-enters the flow

p: Seven roles share the flow. The vendor team, Manuscript Admin and the Author carry most of the manual work before peer review starts.

p.em: Figure AS-2: AS-IS persona view, who does what at each stage

h1: 4. Gaps and concerns in the current flow
p: Seven gaps slow the manuscript before peer review starts. Gaps 1 to 5 come from the AS-IS slides; gaps 6 and 7 also draw on the Triage and Routing future-state product definition.

td.p: Quality and integrity checks run late
iThenticate, Fundref, profile and data checks run during peer review, after editors are already engaged
Manuscript Admin and vendor teams run the admin check; missing items go on hold while the author is contacted
Every compliance hit becomes a ticket
Each OFAC or RRS / funder hit raises a ServiceNow ticket that a vendor validates, false positives included
Work is split across four systems
Publishing Center, Paragon Plus, ServiceNow and DOTS each hold part of the status; flags sit outside the ticket
Single system and flow, error rate
Seven roles touch a manuscript; a flagged one can pass vendor, Portfolio Services, Legal and Manuscript Admin
Assign EE is a manual first task; the choice leans on raw open-assignment counts and context spread over screens
Wrong routes and transfers are hard to fix
Transfer has no defined destination in the flow; a wrong assignment is undone by unsubmission or a workaround

p.em: Impact ratings are a first assessment for discussion, not from the deck.

p: Further concerns read from the AS-IS flow, to confirm with the business owners:

li.p: No baseline. Volumes, touch counts, false-positive rates and stage times are not measured end to end, so improvement targets cannot be set yet.
Revisions repeat the work. A revised or resubmitted manuscript takes a Full Check and the vendor re-runs iThenticate and funding checks, so the same effort is spent again.
Reference data is maintained by hand. The SDN, inclusion and exclusion lists and the funder / AAM technical sheet sit outside the workflow; the checks are only as current as these lists.
Fragmented audit trail. Outcomes, flags and notes for the EO are split between Paragon Plus and ServiceNow tickets, which makes compliance reporting and root-cause analysis harder.
Dependence on the vendor queue. Throughput before peer review is bounded by vendor capacity on tickets and admin checks.
Author experience. Problems reach the author late and one at a time, through outreach, rather than as one itemised report at upload.

h1: 5. Potential scope of improvement in the TO-BE flow
p: The proposed TO-BE flow validates once and routes automatically: checks move to the point of upload, the ticket queue is removed for routine cases, and editors are selected by rules in one flow from Publishing Center to DOTS.

p.em: Figure AS-3: AS-IS gaps mapped to the three proposed automation measures

td.p: Replaces late checks and the manual admin check

li.p: Rules engine with generic rules plus journal-specific rules
Checks plagiarism, integrity, figures, graphs, equations and completeness
Integrity score against a pass threshold set per journal
Failures go back to the author at once with an itemised report
First-pass validation rate
Items returned to authors
Defects found after assignment

td.p: Replaces the ServiceNow ticket and vendor validation

li.p: Validation result drives an Accepted or Rejected outcome
Outcome and reasons recorded on the manuscript, not in a ticket
Only exceptions reach a person, such as a confirmed OFAC match to Legal
Accepted manuscripts pass straight to triage and routing
Tickets and vendor touches per manuscript
Upload-to-triage time
False positives overturned

td.p: Replaces manual Assign EE and ad hoc transfer

li.p: Prioritized queue with decision-ready manuscript context
Auto-selection of Associate Editor and Executive Editor by expertise, capacity and conflict rules
Assignment mode per journal: manual, recommended or automatic
Decision support for Accept, Reject, Transfer and Revise, with alternate-journal suggestions
Time to editor assignment
Reassignment and override rate
Submission-to-first-decision time

h2: 5.b What changes from the AS-IS flow

td.p: iThenticate, Fundref, profile and data checks during peer review
Run once, at upload, against generic and journal rules
A ServiceNow ticket per hit, validated by a vendor
Automated Accepted or Rejected outcome; ServiceNow and the vendor queue handle exceptions only
Manual admin check; hold and author outreach loop
Completeness rules at upload; failures returned with an itemised report
Rules select AE and EE by expertise, stage-aware capacity, conflicts and journal rules
System proposes one of 3 to 5 mapped journals, or the Author selects one; the Publishing Editor approves or reassigns; context travels with the manuscript
One record and one status: score, outcome, assignment and audit trail on the manuscript
Full Check and repeated vendor checks

h2: 5.c TO-BE use case from the 11-17 workshop

li.p: The Author uploads the manuscript; the platform checks generic and journal-specific rules and generates an integrity score of 1 to 10.
Score 1 to 5: rejected and returned to the author. Score 6 to 10: passes and is assigned to the Executive Editor with status "Pending Approval".
The EE approves the score and assigns the manuscript for peer review; the reviewer returns Accept, Reject, Revise (minor or major) or Transfer.
Transfer is system driven (proposed from the journal's 3 to 5 mapped journals; the author accepts, or the PE assigns) or author driven (the PE approves or assigns another journal).
Open points: what happens if the EE does not approve the score; whether the author must consent to a journal the PE assigns.

ac:rich-text-body.p: Guardrails. The TO-BE flow is proposed for discussion. An authorized Editor still makes the scientific and editorial decision. AI on manuscript content needs security, legal and privacy approval before any pilot.
Next steps: baseline current volumes, touch counts and stage times; set a target for each measure; pick pilot journals.
